The British first came to New Zealand in October 1769, when British explorer Captain James Cook arrived at Te Tairāwhiti (Poverty Bay) [d3][d8]. Over the following decades, whalers, sealers, and missionaries also came to New Zealand prior to 1840 [d5]. Formal British colonization began with the signing of the Treaty of Waitangi on 6 February 1840, when William Hobson invited Māori chiefs to sign a treaty with the British Crown [d2][d8]. British sovereignty over all of New Zealand was then proclaimed on 21 May 1840, and the Colony of New Zealand was formally established as a separate Crown colony on 3 May 1841 [d1][d2][d4].
